rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis studies HfZrTi(TaNbV)x alloys with varying x, while the hidden target studies equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived single crystals with varying constituent count. These are entirely different alloy systems and types of intervention (compositional series vs. constituent count variation in a different base system).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses as-cast alloys and quasi-static/dynamic compression at 4000 s^-1 in air, whereas the hidden target uses homogenized single crystals compressed at 1e-4 s^-1 from 9 to 1373 K with strain-rate jumps. The conditions are completely different in material state, temperature range, and strain rate.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes BCC stabilization, omega-phase embrittlement, solid-solution strengthening from lattice distortion, adiabatic shear banding, and oxidative fragmentation energy release. The hidden target involves thermally activated glide through solid-solution obstacles, phonon-drag inertial dulling, and Cottrell-type dynamic strain aging. These are entirely different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts BCC stabilization, strength-ductility balance, and dynamic oxidation energy release for HZTX0.9, with brittle fragmentation for HZTX0.1. The hidden target predicts CRSS increase with cooling, inertial dulling below ~77 K, and a Portevin–Le Chatelier peak at high temperature, correlated with MSAD and Mn+Fe content. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
